standard_prerequisites.statement: Finitely satisfiable types over parameter sets smaller than the saturation cardinal are realized; propositional compactness builds linear orders from finite restrictions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Compact expandability/resplendence of saturated models
standard_prerequisites.statement: A saturated model of cardinality kappa admits an expansion satisfying a consistent set of sentences in an expanded language of size at most kappa, allowing fewer than kappa named parameters and free variables replaced by constants. Special-model alternatives are as in the source Remark7.3.

core_obligations: Build downward HF-closures and normalize/interpolate HF-orders without introducing a second earlier block.
Use finite binary-tree constructions and saturation to produce fresh elements that extend a closed parameter set strongly.
Prove strong partial isomorphisms uniquely extend to their generated Steiner substructures.
Extend an isomorphism over a countable strong substructure through a finite or infinite downward closure, preserving all partial triple relations and strongness.
In the infinite closure case, construct finite approximations, formulate the five-part expansion type, prove finite satisfiability and recover closedness after realization.

proof_roadmap.step: Establish HF-closure and order-moving lemmas needed to preserve strong embeddings.
Build fresh strong points by binary trees and extend isomorphisms over generated closures.
Choose a suitable saturated order expansion and solve the trivial and finite closure cases.
For infinite closure, construct finite partial approximations and the expanded-language type; verify its realization remains closed and extends to generated substructures.

difficulty_reason: The counted target is a full homogeneity/back-and-forth mechanism for a nonstandard class of infinite incidence algebras. Even with ordinary saturation and compact expandability allowed, it requires custom strong closures, tree-based fresh-point constructions, preservation of unique block constraints, and a finite-approximation argument for infinite downward closures whose order expansion must prevent additional predecessor products. The final back-and-forth is not available by a generic homogeneity theorem: those structural and type-consistency obligations are included in the solution.

compared.difference: The published item is only finite binary-tree existence above a point. It is now an uncounted support lemma; the new target is the back-and-forth system for arbitrary countable strong substructures.

editorial_notes: C_un denotes the class of finite unconfined partial Steiner triple systems (source437-440). In the counted theorem a substructure is closed under the quasigroup operation, as the author parenthesis explicitly says; partial systems occur at intermediate stages.

The external HF-ordering proof is supplied from the same authors, Endomorphisms of free Steiner quasigroups, fixed version2412.06055v3, Proposition3.11. It is a solution component and is separately attributed.

The external proof formula294 prints totality for all a,b, including a=b, although the intended strict total order requires a!=b; the main paper prints that restriction explicitly in the same compactness argument at780. Both source passages remain unmodified.
The natural HF-order on a tree orders parents above children; reversing it orders the root first, as used by source820-823.

For Case3 the finite variables are permuted according to their source HF-order before the b_j construction, as explicitly stated at967; they are assigned back to the corresponding x_i. No mathematical formula in the author proof is replaced.
Use fixed v3, which the authors identify as a post-publication correction of the finite-tree proof and main Case3. Do not substitute v1/v2 or a published PDF with the earlier proof.

source_authorship.known_AI_disclosure: No AI-assistance declaration located in the read source; no assertion about undisclosed author tools.

review_checkpoints: Strongness supplies an HF-order with the parameter substructure first, and downward closure is countable because each point introduces at most two immediate predecessors.

In the finite approximation step a new point is either the forced product of two available smaller points, a product with a parameter, or a fresh strong point. The HF-order prevents two conflicting predecessor products.

The five conditions of Sigma encode the triple diagram, relative order, and absence of new smaller products both for old parameters and genuinely free new nodes; merely realizing the triple diagram would not suffice.
The generated-closure extension lemma ensures that after obtaining closed partial systems, the map extends to actual substructures required by the theorem.

issues_for_independent_review.detail: Independently evaluate the full stated claim and this exact proof chain, not just the previously published tree lemma or the final short completeness corollary.
Confirm compact expandability is an acceptable standard input and check finite consistency/closedness, which remain the target proof obligations.
The missing a!=b restriction in the strict-order encoding is explicitly present in the main article780; review the annotated interpretation without changing author text.
Comparison required before ready; the authors themselves disclose a closely related general incidence-structure theorem.

The author chooses a saturated ordered expansion of the same cardinality in930. Check the exact standard expansion theorem and the special-model alternative924; merely assuming saturation of the reduct must not be used as an unjustified arbitrary-theory same-cardinality saturation principle. This is a review question, not an established counterexample.

editorial_scope: One counted back-and-forth theorem. All nonstandard HF-order, tree, fresh-point and generated-isomorphism lemmas used are included in the solution chain. No separate task is counted for the already published finite-tree lemma or for completeness/stability corollaries. The second source supplies the actual author proof of the HF-ordering criterion. Saturation/compact expandability are explicit standard model-theoretic inputs.
